title: Microsoft president explains company's $10 million White House ballroom donation
summary: On Face the Nation, Margaret Brennan presses Microsoft president Brad Smith on the company's day-long global outage, and he apologises, rules out AI or hacking as the cause, and explains how AI-driven bug hunting is forcing a risky, rapid upgrade of the world's older software. Smith then weighs a proposed tax on data centres built abroad, agreeing that cutting-edge AI training may belong in the US but arguing that ordinary cloud services must sit close to their customers. The interview closes with questions about ByteDance's spending on Microsoft's AI services and Microsoft's donation to the White House ballroom, which Smith frames as part of a consistent, bipartisan approach to government.
focus: Shadow Smith's opening answer explaining the outage as a combination of an older and a newer software update, then his short analogy comparing data centres to local power plants serving a city.

vocab.meaning: a period when a service or system stops working
vocab.context: Brennan opened by asking about the day-long Microsoft service failure that hit businesses around the world earlier in November.
vocab.example: A four-hour payments outage on Black Friday cost the retailer more than its entire annual IT budget.

vocab.meaning: badly limited or slowed down, unable to work normally
vocab.context: Brennan described companies, including newsrooms, as crippled in their daily work while the systems were down.
vocab.example: Hobbled by a fragmented ERP landscape, the client could not close its books in under three weeks.

vocab.meaning: a deliberate attempt to damage or break into computer systems
vocab.context: Smith stressed that the failure was neither caused by AI nor by hackers deliberately targeting Microsoft.
vocab.example: The board asked us to quantify the revenue at risk from a major cyberattack on the logistics platform.

vocab.meaning: a weakness that can be exploited to cause harm
vocab.context: Brennan asked whether AI tools that hunt for software weaknesses are creating more fixes than old systems can safely absorb.
vocab.example: Our diligence flagged a single-supplier vulnerability that could halt production for six weeks.

vocab.meaning: to fix a problem in software by installing a small update
vocab.context: Smith urged ordinary users and companies alike to install security fixes quickly as AI speeds up the discovery of flaws.
vocab.example: Rather than patch the old pricing engine yet again, we recommended replacing it within eighteen months.

vocab.meaning: old but still in use, and often hard to update or replace
vocab.context: Smith said organisations need to modernise the ageing systems that are most likely to break when updates arrive quickly.
vocab.example: Roughly 40% of the bank's run cost goes on maintaining legacy core systems.

vocab.meaning: planned and done together by several people or groups
vocab.zh: 协同一致的；齐心协力的
vocab.context: Smith called for joint effort between government and the tech industry to share information on threats.
vocab.example: Turning around customer churn will take a concerted push from sales, product and service, not a single campaign.

vocab.meaning: openness about what happened and why, with nothing hidden
vocab.context: Smith pointed to Microsoft's detailed public reports as evidence it was being open about the incident.
vocab.example: Investors rewarded the company's transparency about the restructuring costs with a higher multiple.

vocab.meaning: similar in a way that makes a comparison useful
vocab.context: Smith said the idea of keeping AI model training in America was comparable to the government's approach to advanced chips.
vocab.example: The client's subscription shift is analogous to what the software industry went through a decade ago.

vocab.meaning: a small but important difference or detail
vocab.context: Smith added that the tax idea needed more subtlety because most data centres simply serve local customers.
vocab.example: The headline number is right, but the nuance is that two-thirds of the growth came from price, not volume.

vocab.meaning: involving or supported by both main political parties
vocab.context: Smith said Microsoft takes the same even-handed approach whichever party is in power.
vocab.example: A bipartisan infrastructure bill would give the client far more certainty for its ten-year capex plan.

vocab.meaning: a person or organisation that gives money to a cause or project
vocab.context: Brennan noted reports that Microsoft's contribution to the White House ballroom made it one of the biggest givers.
vocab.example: As a major donor to the university, the firm had to recuse itself from the campus advisory tender.

phrases.meaning: a rare combination of several bad factors that together cause a crisis
phrases.zh: 多重不利因素叠加；完美风暴
phrases.context: Smith used this image to explain how an old update, a new update and a traffic shift combined to bring services down.
phrases.example: Rising rates, a supplier default and a weak holiday season created a perfect storm for the retailer.

phrases.context: Smith compared local data centres to local power plants that keep a city functioning, arguing both must be close to customers.
phrases.example: Most of the IT budget goes on keeping the lights on, leaving little for real transformation.

phrases.meaning: a decision that depends on personal opinion because there is no clearly right answer
phrases.zh: 主观判断；需权衡的决定
phrases.context: Smith framed decisions about working with an administration as matters that require weighing each case.
phrases.example: Whether to exit the Brazilian market now or wait a year is ultimately a judgment call for the board.

phrases.meaning: to keep a distance from or openly disagree with others
phrases.context: Smith said Microsoft cooperates with governments where it can but distances itself when it disagrees.
phrases.example: We advised the client to stand apart from the industry lobby on the emissions rule to protect its brand.

phrases.meaning: to give your opinion or use your influence in a discussion or decision
phrases.zh: 发表意见；参与（讨论或决定）
phrases.context: Brennan asked whether Microsoft had a say in the ballroom project after giving money to it.
phrases.example: Before we finalise the target operating model, the CFO will want to weigh in on the finance org design.
